partners.mechanism_chain: NCF1 (HGNC:7727) —DISRUPTS→ NADPH oxidase complex (GO:0005917); CYBB (HGNC:2404) —DISRUPTS→ NADPH oxidase complex (GO:0005917); NADPH oxidase complex (GO:0005917) —DECREASES→ Reactive Oxygen Species production (GO:0009800); Reactive Oxygen Species production (GO:0009800) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal granuloma formation (HP:0002714); Reactive Oxygen Species production (GO:0009800) —LEADS_TO→ Impaired bactericidal activity (HP:00114223). Loss-of-function mutations in either NCF1 (AR form) or CYBB (X-linked form) lead to a dysfunctional NADPH oxidase complex. This impairs the production of reactive oxygen species (ROS) by phagocytes, resulting in increased susceptibility to infections and the characteristic granuloma formation seen in chronic granulomatous disease.

partners.diseaseBName: granulomatous disease, chronic, autosomal recessive, cytochrome b-positive, type 2
partners.mechanism_chain: NCF1 (HGNC:7717) —DISRUPTS→ NADPH oxidase complex assembly and function (GO:0032080); NCF2 (HGNC:7718) —DISRUPTS→ NADPH oxidase complex assembly and function (GO:0032080); NADPH oxidase complex assembly and function (GO:0032080) —LEADS_TO→ Recurrent infections (HP:00114210); NADPH oxidase complex assembly and function (GO:0032080) —LEADS_TO→ Granuloma formation (HP:0002698); NADPH oxidase complex assembly and function (GO:0032080) —LEADS_TO→ Neutrophil dysfunction (HP:0005413). partners.mechanism_chain: NCF1 (HGNC:7726) —DISRUPTS→ NADPH oxidase complex assembly and function (GO:0005913); NADPH oxidase complex assembly and function (GO:0005913) —LEADS_TO→ Granulomatous inflammation (HP:0002670); ATP7A (HGNC:773) —DISRUPTS→ Copper transport and homeostasis (GO:0006811); Copper transport and homeostasis (GO:0006811) —DECREASES→ Lysosomal function (GO:0005704); Lysosomal function (GO:0005704) —DISRUPTS→ Oxidative stress response (GO:0006974); Oxidative stress response (GO:0006974) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal connective tissue (HP:0003499); Oxidative stress response (GO:0006974) —LEADS_TO→ Neurological abnormalities (HP:0000707). Loss-of-function variants in NCF1 disrupt NADPH oxidase complex function, leading to impaired phagocyte function and granulomatous inflammation. Concurrently, loss-of-function variants in ATP7A disrupt copper transport, affecting numerous copper-dependent enzymes and processes. This disruption in copper homeostasis impacts lysosomal function, which in turn exacerbates oxidative stress. The resulting cellular dysfunction and oxidative stress contribute to shared downstream phenotypes such as neurological abnormalities and abnormal connective tissue development, which can manifest in both conditions.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the convergence on cellular oxidative stress and lysosomal dysfunction could reveal common therapeutic targets for these otherwise distinct rare diseases, such as agents that modulate oxidative stress or enhance lysosomal function.
